items.decision: Journey 1, setup over several repositories: run from a folder outside every repository, setup walks 3 listed repositories, asks only for missing values, and reports each one as complete, asked or failed.
items.evidence: R-1: J-1 accept. Story 1 and the cited criteria state every observable this journey checks: asks only what is missing, acts on the given repository from any folder, warns on a local override, and goes on after one repository fails. items.decision: Journey 11, an ordinary agent session: it reads only its own repository's settings and accounts, and writes working files only into that repository's spec folder, whatever note-taking app is set.

items.decision: Role-based access: which roles, and where is each refusal proven? Answer: Triggered. Roles: the developer in their own terminal, an agent session, a teammate. The agent side is proven by the text the agent receives (journeys 2, 3, 8); the side below it by the creator, the guard and the secret step (round 2). Two actions have no refusal below the instructions in your signed design, editing the list and writing team settings on the agent's own initiative; they get an instruction check only, with that reason recorded.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-1 accept. (SDD.md:267-281; PRD.md:156-165)

items.decision: Data scope: what is the scope and where is it proven? Answer: Triggered. The scope is one repository and one machine; there is no company or vendor scope. Proven by journey 11 (a session sees only its repository), journey 6 (a teammate sees no personal value) and journey 1 (only the walk reads other repositories).

Input validation: which inputs, and where proven? Answer: Triggered. Every root rule (journey 10), the list's refusals (journey 4), an unknown short name (journey 5), a matching site key (journey 8), and one contract row per refusal in round 2.

Audit history of new database records: does it apply? Answer: Not applicable: the feature adds no database table or entity. Everything it stores is a file under the home folder or a repository's git folder.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-4 accept. (SDD.md:285-291)

items.decision: Deep links and state in the page address: does it apply? Answer: Not applicable: there is no web page. The surfaces are commands, hooks and the guard.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-5 accept. (SDD.md:123)

items.decision: Accepted staples: does it apply? Answer: Not applicable: this plugin has no staples registry, and the PRD accepted none.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-6 accept. (PRD.md:192)

items.decision: State owned elsewhere that can change between a check and the action it guards: which windows, and how is each covered? Answer: Triggered, 5 windows. A forge token removed after setup checked it: the call fails with account not available (journey 3). A session starting in a worktree between the setup list and its removal: liveness is read again at removal and the guard checks again (journey 9). The harness rewriting its settings file while the secret step waits: refused, nothing changed (journey 8). A confirmed root that later becomes a repository: the rules run on every read (journey 10). A worktree changing branch between the copy-deletion check and the deletion in the same run: accepted, because the report lists each deleted value so you can type it back.

Two writers at once: does it apply? Answer: Applies. A second writer on a changed file refuses and changes nothing; a lock held past 2000 ms fails naming the file; on Windows a busy file swap retries 10 times at 50 ms. One contract row each in round 2.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-8 accept. (SDD.md:431-433)

items.decision: Repeating an action: does it apply? Answer: Applies. A second run asks nothing (journey 1); adding a listed path is refused (journey 4); rerunning the secret step replaces the value and keeps one backup (journey 8); a run stopped after writing a short-name marker reuses it (round 2).
Pages and sort order: does it apply? Answer: Not applicable: no surface returns results in pages.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-10 accept. (SDD.md:123-140)

items.decision: Allowed state changes: does it apply? Answer: Applies. A forge account goes from unset to saved only after the host accepts it (journey 3). The root migration keeps both keys until deletion, and the new one wins (journey 9). A Jira sign-in goes from absent to stored to replaced, only through the secret step (journey 8).

Shape of error answers: does it apply? Answer: Applies. Exit 3 with the ERROR= line naming the rule and /afk:setup for a root failure; exit 1 for any other creator failure; the guard's refusal text; account not available. One contract row each in round 2.
items.evidence: R-1: AS-12 accept. (SDD.md:129-138)

header.fork:
The verification set is settled. Nothing on this page needs an answer.

Form: one black-box acceptance test file that drives every entry point in a sandbox, plus a live-run list. This feature's first subtask adds the unit, smoke and static tiers to the committed AFK file.

Journeys: 11, covering all 7 stories and all 48 acceptance criteria (round 1 said 55: a miscount). Contract checks: 22, one per contract row and per module with no row; each protected surface has its refused-agent test.

Cross-cutting checks: role access, data scope, input validation, state owned elsewhere, concurrency, repeats, state changes and error shape apply; audit history, deep links, staples and paging do not, each with its reason.

Live-run list, environment-limited: a second real GitHub account, an Enterprise Server host, a real GitLab host, real Jira sites, the Claude Code worktree tool and its hook, folder trust, a second Windows drive.

Gaps for the plan: the final gate expects a running app (a plugin issue to draft, with your approval); CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and the secret step; CI does not run the two worktree smoke scripts; how setup detects the Codex app; the bare secret-step exit status.
